library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hosoi_2026_levofloxacin_plasma_mouse"))$reference`
* Article: [Antimicrob Agents Chemother 2026;70(8):e0037526](https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.00375-26)
* Supplemental Material (Figures S1-S6, Tables S1-S6): <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.00375-26>

Hosoi and colleagues compared three fluoroquinolones with very different
penetration into the pulmonary epithelial lining fluid (ELF) under identical
conditions in a neutropenic murine *Streptococcus pneumoniae* lung infection
model. For each drug they fitted a one-compartment model with first-order
subcutaneous absorption to the plasma concentrations and, separately, to the
ELF concentrations, and related the 24 h change in lung bacterial burden to
plasma- and ELF-based PK/PD indices with a sigmoid inhibitory Imax model.
AUC/MIC was the index most strongly correlated with the antibacterial effect in
both matrices.

The paper contributes six models, one per drug and matrix, because the plasma
and ELF data were fitted separately and each has its own Imax fit:

| Drug | Plasma model | ELF model |
|---|---|---|
| Levofloxacin (LVFX) | `Hosoi_2026_levofloxacin_plasma_mouse` | `Hosoi_2026_levofloxacin_elf_mouse` |
| Garenoxacin (GRNX) | `Hosoi_2026_garenoxacin_plasma_mouse` | `Hosoi_2026_garenoxacin_elf_mouse` |
| Lascufloxacin (LSFX) | `Hosoi_2026_lascufloxacin_plasma_mouse` | `Hosoi_2026_lascufloxacin_elf_mouse` |

Each model carries the PK, the MIC of the study strain, a 24 h AUC accumulator
(`fauc_0_24` of free plasma drug, or `auc_elf_0_24` of total ELF drug), the
index (`fauc_mic` or `auc_mic`) and the Imax output `dlog10cfu`, the change in
lung burden in log10 CFU/lung over the 24 h treatment window.

# Population

Female ddY mice (5 weeks old on arrival, used after one week of acclimation)
were rendered neutropenic with cyclophosphamide (150 mg/kg IP on day -4 and
100 mg/kg on day -1) and inoculated intratracheally with about 1e7 CFU of
*S. pneumoniae* ATCC 49619 (Materials and Methods, 'Animals'). The MICs were
0.512 mg/L for levofloxacin and 0.032 mg/L for garenoxacin and lascufloxacin
(Results). For PK, single subcutaneous doses (LVFX 50, 100 and 200 mg/kg;
GRNX 30, 60 and 120 mg/kg; LSFX 10, 20 and 30 mg/kg) were given and three mice
per time point were sampled destructively at 5-300 min; ELF concentrations
were derived from bronchoalveolar lavage by the urea dilution method. For PD,
various subcutaneous regimens were given from 2 to 26 h after infection and the
lungs were harvested at 26 h. The same information is available
programmatically, e.g.
`readModelDb("Hosoi_2026_garenoxacin_elf_mouse")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every value in the six `ini()` blocks carries an in-file comment with its
source location. Summary:

| Element | Source |
|---|---|
| One-compartment model, first-order absorption, plasma and ELF fitted separately | Materials and Methods, 'Pharmacokinetic analysis' |
| `lka`, `lcl`, `lvc` (plasma) and `lka`, `lcl_elf`, `lv_elf` (ELF) | Tables S1 (LVFX), S2 (GRNX), S3 (LSFX), 'Mean' rows |
| `fu` = 1 - %PB/100 (0.845, 0.114, 0.354) | Results, 'Plasma and ELF pharmacokinetics' |
| `mic` (0.512, 0.032, 0.032 mg/L) | Results, 'MIC' |
| ELF concentration by urea dilution | Materials and Methods, equation 2 |
| Imax equation `E = E0 - Imax * X^gamma / (X^gamma + IC50^gamma)` | Materials and Methods, equation 3 |
| `e0`, `limax`, `lic50`, `lhill` (AUC/MIC column) | Tables S4 (LVFX), S5 (GRNX), S6 (LSFX) |
| Stasis, 1-log10 and 2-log10 kill targets | Tables 2-4 |
| Human ELF penetration ratios and adjusted targets | Table 5 |

# Simulation

Typical single-dose profiles at the paper's PK doses. The models have no
between-animal variability, so one subject per dose is enough. Observation rows
sit on the drug-holding state (`central` or `elf`).

```{r models}
drugs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug,           ~abbr,  ~doses,
  "levofloxacin",  "LVFX", c(50, 100, 200),
  "garenoxacin",   "GRNX", c(30, 60, 120),
  "lascufloxacin", "LSFX", c(10, 20, 30)
)
model_name <- function(drug, matrix) paste0("Hosoi_2026_", drug, "_", matrix, "_mouse")
obs_state <- c(plasma = "central", elf = "elf")

make_events <- function(doses, matrix, times) {
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(doses), function(i) {
    bind_rows(
      data.frame(id = i, time = 0, amt = doses[i], evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
      data.frame(id = i, time = times, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = obs_state[[matrix]])
    )
  })) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

solve_model <- function(drug, matrix, doses, times) {
  ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(model_name(drug, matrix)))
  # The models carry no between-animal variability, so rxode2 warns that a
  # multi-subject solve has no omega; that is intended, and only that warning
  # is muffled.
  s <- withCallingHandlers(
    as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(ui, events = make_events(doses, matrix, times))),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
  conc <- if (matrix == "plasma") s$Cc else s$Celf
  index <- if (matrix == "plasma") s$fauc_mic else s$auc_mic
  data.frame(
    drug = drug, matrix = matrix, id = s$id, dose = doses[s$id], time = s$time,
    conc = conc, free = if (matrix == "plasma") s$Cu else s$Celf,
    index = index, dlog10cfu = s$dlog10cfu
  )
}

grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 1, by = 1 / 60), seq(1, 24, by = 0.1))))
sim <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(drugs)), function(i) {
  bind_rows(lapply(c("plasma", "elf"), function(m) {
    solve_model(drugs$drug[i], m, drugs$doses[[i]], grid)
  }))
})) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(drug, matrix, dose, "mg/kg"))

stopifnot(!anyNA(sim$conc), all(sim$conc >= 0))
```

```{r profiles, fig.height = 6}
sim |>
  filter(time <= 5) |>
  mutate(matrix = ifelse(matrix == "plasma", "Plasma (total)", "ELF")) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc, colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(matrix ~ drug, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after subcutaneous dose (h)", y = "Concentration (mg/L)",
    colour = "Dose (mg/kg)",
    caption = "Typical single-dose profiles over the 5-300 min sampling window of the PK study."
  )
```

The paper shows the fits only as observed-versus-predicted and
residual plots (Figures S1-S6), so there is no concentration-time figure to
overlay.

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA values. PKNCA is run on the simulated single-dose
profiles, and its AUC0-inf and half-life are checked against the closed forms
of the one-compartment model, Dose / CL and ln(2) * V / CL (the absorption rate
constant exceeds the elimination rate constant in every fit, so the terminal
phase is elimination).

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(conc)) |>
  select(treatment, id, time, conc)
dose_df <- sim |>
  distinct(treatment, id, dose) |>
  mutate(time = 0)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, conc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, dose ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

params <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(drugs)), function(i) {
  bind_rows(lapply(c("plasma", "elf"), function(m) {
    ini_df <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(model_name(drugs$drug[i], m)))$iniDf
    v <- setNames(exp(ini_df$est), ini_df$name)
    cl <- if (m == "plasma") v[["lcl"]] else v[["lcl_elf"]]
    vd <- if (m == "plasma") v[["lvc"]] else v[["lv_elf"]]
    data.frame(
      treatment = paste(drugs$drug[i], m, drugs$doses[[i]], "mg/kg"),
      auc_cf = drugs$doses[[i]] / cl, thalf_cf = log(2) * vd / cl
    )
  }))
}))

nca_check <- left_join(nca_wide, params, by = "treatment")
nca_check |>
  rename(
    Treatment = treatment, "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-inf (mg.h/L)" = aucinf.obs, "t1/2 (h)" = half.life,
    "Dose/CL (mg.h/L)" = auc_cf, "ln2 V/CL (h)" = thalf_cf
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "PKNCA on the simulated single-dose profiles against the one-compartment closed forms.")

stopifnot(
  # Same drawn parameters on both sides: the gap is numerical (trapezoids on a
  # 1-6 min grid plus a log-linear extrapolation), so a tight bound is correct.
  all(abs(nca_check$aucinf.obs / nca_check$auc_cf - 1) < 0.02),
  all(abs(nca_check$half.life / nca_check$thalf_cf - 1) < 0.02)
)
```

# ELF penetration in the mouse

The model AUC ratio ELF / free plasma is a property of the PK alone. Because
the indices of the PD regimens were computed from these models, the same ratio
reappears in the Imax fits: for garenoxacin and lascufloxacin the ELF fit is
the plasma fit with the index rescaled (Imax, E0 and gamma agree to two
decimals, Tables S5 and S6), so the ELF IC50 divided by the plasma IC50 must
equal the model penetration ratio. This is a check on the PK and the PD
transcription together.

```{r penetration}
auc24 <- sim |>
  filter(abs(time - 24) < 1e-8) |>
  mutate(auc = index * ifelse(drug == "levofloxacin", 0.512, 0.032)) |>
  select(drug, matrix, dose, auc) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = matrix, values_from = auc) |>
  group_by(drug) |>
  summarise(model_ratio = mean(elf / plasma), .groups = "drop")

ic50 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug,           ~ic50_plasma, ~ic50_elf, ~imax_plasma, ~imax_elf,
  "levofloxacin",  58.59,        125.08,    5.61,         6.82,
  "garenoxacin",   22.91,        351.50,    4.05,         4.05,
  "lascufloxacin", 18.47,        165.57,    3.27,         3.27
) |>
  mutate(ic50_ratio = ic50_elf / ic50_plasma)

pen <- left_join(auc24, ic50, by = "drug") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (model_ratio / ic50_ratio - 1))
pen |>
  select(drug, model_ratio, ic50_ratio, pct_diff) |>
  rename(
    Drug = drug, "Model AUC_ELF / fAUC_plasma" = model_ratio,
    "IC50 ELF / IC50 plasma (Tables S4-S6)" = ic50_ratio, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Murine ELF penetration: PK models against the Imax fits.")

stopifnot(
  # Deterministic. Lascufloxacin agrees to 0.2% and garenoxacin to 3%;
  # levofloxacin's two Imax fits do not share Imax or gamma, so its plasma and
  # ELF indices were not a pure rescaling and agree only to about 6%.
  abs(pen$pct_diff[pen$drug == "lascufloxacin"]) < 1,
  abs(pen$pct_diff[pen$drug == "garenoxacin"]) < 5,
  abs(pen$pct_diff[pen$drug == "levofloxacin"]) < 10
)
```

The ordering matches the paper's account: levofloxacin barely concentrates in
mouse ELF (about 2-fold over free plasma), lascufloxacin about 9-fold and
garenoxacin about 15-fold, largely because garenoxacin is 88.6% bound in mouse
plasma.

# Replicate published figures and targets

A sweep of single subcutaneous doses through each model gives the index and the
24 h `dlog10cfu` read at t = 24 h, which traces the fitted curve of panels A
(plasma fAUC/MIC) and D (ELF AUC/MIC) of Figures 1-3.

```{r sweep}
sweep_doses <- exp(seq(log(0.1), log(2000), length.out = 200))
sweep <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(drugs)), function(i) {
  bind_rows(lapply(c("plasma", "elf"), function(m) {
    solve_model(drugs$drug[i], m, sweep_doses, c(0, 24))
  }))
})) |>
  filter(time == 24)
```

```{r fig-curves, fig.height = 5.5}
xmax <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug,           ~matrix,  ~xmax,
  "levofloxacin",  "plasma", 100,
  "levofloxacin",  "elf",    200,
  "garenoxacin",   "plasma", 120,
  "garenoxacin",   "elf",    2000,
  "lascufloxacin", "plasma", 400,
  "lascufloxacin", "elf",    3000
)
sweep |>
  left_join(xmax, by = c("drug", "matrix")) |>
  filter(index <= xmax) |>
  mutate(matrix = ifelse(matrix == "plasma", "Plasma fAUC/MIC", "ELF AUC/MIC")) |>
  ggplot(aes(index, dlog10cfu)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(matrix ~ drug, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    x = "AUC/MIC over 24 h", y = "Change in log10 CFU/lung",
    caption = "Replicates the fitted curves of Figures 1A/1D, 2A/2D and 3A/3D of Hosoi 2026."
  )
```

Interpolating the sweep at a change of 0, -1 and -2 log10 CFU/lung gives the
exposure targets, compared below with Tables 2-4.

```{r targets}
published_targets <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug,           ~matrix,  ~endpoint,     ~published,
  "levofloxacin",  "plasma", "stasis",       13.1,
  "levofloxacin",  "plasma", "1-log10 kill", 30.6,
  "levofloxacin",  "plasma", "2-log10 kill", 53.0,
  "levofloxacin",  "elf",    "stasis",       19.5,
  "levofloxacin",  "elf",    "1-log10 kill", 48.6,
  "levofloxacin",  "elf",    "2-log10 kill", 88.6,
  "garenoxacin",   "plasma", "stasis",       13.8,
  "garenoxacin",   "plasma", "1-log10 kill", 22.8,
  "garenoxacin",   "plasma", "2-log10 kill", 37.5,
  "garenoxacin",   "elf",    "stasis",       215.7,
  "garenoxacin",   "elf",    "1-log10 kill", 351.8,
  "garenoxacin",   "elf",    "2-log10 kill", 573.9,
  "lascufloxacin", "plasma", "stasis",       10.0,
  "lascufloxacin", "plasma", "1-log10 kill", 16.5,
  "lascufloxacin", "plasma", "2-log10 kill", 22.8,
  "lascufloxacin", "elf",    "stasis",       90.1,
  "lascufloxacin", "elf",    "1-log10 kill", 147.7,
  "lascufloxacin", "elf",    "2-log10 kill", 204.0
)
effect_level <- c("stasis" = 0, "1-log10 kill" = -1, "2-log10 kill" = -2)

targets <- published_targets |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(simulated = {
    s <- sweep[sweep$drug == drug & sweep$matrix == matrix, ]
    s <- s[order(s$dlog10cfu), ]
    exp(approx(s$dlog10cfu, log(s$index), xout = effect_level[[endpoint]])$y)
  }) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated / published - 1))

targets |>
  rename(
    Drug = drug, Matrix = matrix, Endpoint = endpoint,
    "Published (Tables 2-4)" = published, "Simulated" = simulated, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "AUC/MIC targets for stasis, 1-log10 and 2-log10 kill.")

stopifnot(
  # The Imax curve is evaluated through the full PK solve; the residual gap is
  # the rounding of the printed Imax parameters and targets (at most 0.7%).
  all(abs(targets$pct_diff) < 2)
)
```

## Translation to human plasma targets (Table 5)

The paper divides the murine ELF AUC/MIC target by the human ELF penetration
ratio AUC_ELF / fAUC_plasma reported in the literature (1.16, 5.38 and 61.7 for
LVFX, GRNX and LSFX) to obtain a human fAUC_plasma/MIC target.

```{r table5}
human_ratio <- c(levofloxacin = 1.16, garenoxacin = 5.38, lascufloxacin = 61.7)
table5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug,           ~endpoint,      ~published,
  "levofloxacin",  "1-log10 kill", 41.9,
  "levofloxacin",  "2-log10 kill", 76.4,
  "garenoxacin",   "1-log10 kill", 65.4,
  "garenoxacin",   "2-log10 kill", 106.7,
  "lascufloxacin", "1-log10 kill", 2.39,
  "lascufloxacin", "2-log10 kill", 3.31
) |>
  left_join(
    targets |> filter(matrix == "elf") |> select(drug, endpoint, simulated),
    by = c("drug", "endpoint")
  ) |>
  mutate(adjusted = simulated / human_ratio[drug], pct_diff = 100 * (adjusted / published - 1))

table5 |>
  select(drug, endpoint, published, adjusted, pct_diff) |>
  rename(
    Drug = drug, Endpoint = endpoint, "Published adjusted target (Table 5)" = published,
    "From the ELF model" = adjusted, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Human fAUC_plasma/MIC targets predicted from the murine ELF models.")

stopifnot(all(abs(table5$pct_diff) < 2))
```

# Transcription check of all eighteen Imax fits

The paper fitted three indices in each matrix (Tables S4-S6) and tabulated the
resulting targets (Tables 2-4). Only the AUC/MIC fits are packaged, but every
fit is checked here in closed form: equation 3 evaluated at the printed target
should give 0, -1 and -2 log10 CFU/lung.

```{r all-fits}
fits <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug, ~matrix, ~index, ~imax, ~ic50, ~e0, ~gamma, ~stasis, ~kill1, ~kill2,
  "LVFX", "plasma", "fAUC/MIC",  5.61,  58.59, 0.61,  1.41,  13.1,  30.6,  53.0,
  "LVFX", "plasma", "fT>MIC",    3.93,  18.43, 0.80,  2.33,  10.2,  17.1,  27.1,
  "LVFX", "plasma", "fCmax/MIC", 3.12,   9.18, 0.43,  3.21,   5.2,   8.7,  13.6,
  "LVFX", "ELF",    "AUC/MIC",   6.82, 125.08, 0.76,  1.12,  19.5,  48.6,  88.6,
  "LVFX", "ELF",    "T>MIC",    17.73, 313.04, 0.60,  1.23,  20.5,  47.9,  74.9,
  "LVFX", "ELF",    "Cmax/MIC",  3.11,  55.71, 0.40,  3.63,   3.4,   5.4,   8.0,
  "GRNX", "plasma", "fAUC/MIC",  4.05,  22.91, 1.02,  2.17,  13.8,  22.8,  37.5,
  "GRNX", "plasma", "fT>MIC",    4.00,  35.50, 0.86,  2.25,  20.0,  33.4,  53.4,
  "GRNX", "plasma", "fCmax/MIC", 4.07,   2.37, 0.99,  1.58,   1.2,   2.3,  28.9,
  "GRNX", "ELF",    "AUC/MIC",   4.05, 351.50, 1.03,  2.21, 215.7, 351.8, 573.9,
  "GRNX", "ELF",    "T>MIC",     3.29,  53.53, 1.22, 10.00,  50.8,  57.6,  78.7,
  "GRNX", "ELF",    "Cmax/MIC",  4.04,  55.75, 0.97,  1.41,  24.7,  53.9, 114.8,
  "LSFX", "plasma", "fAUC/MIC",  3.27,  18.47, 0.27,  3.93,  10.0,  16.5,  22.8,
  "LSFX", "plasma", "fT>MIC",    3.21,  21.70, 0.26,  5.09,  13.5,  19.9,  25.8,
  "LSFX", "plasma", "fCmax/MIC", 4.14,   3.77, 0.66,  1.09,   0.8,   2.6,   6.5,
  "LSFX", "ELF",    "AUC/MIC",   3.27, 165.57, 0.27,  3.94,  90.1, 147.7, 204.0,
  "LSFX", "ELF",    "T>MIC",     8.71, 128.02, 0.78,  1.02,  13.1,  33.6,  60.8,
  "LSFX", "ELF",    "Cmax/MIC",  4.15,  40.60, 0.67,  1.08,   8.8,  28.1,  70.1
)
imax_effect <- function(x, e0, imax, ic50, gamma) e0 - imax * x^gamma / (x^gamma + ic50^gamma)

fit_check <- fits |>
  mutate(
    "E at stasis" = imax_effect(stasis, e0, imax, ic50, gamma),
    "E at 1-log" = imax_effect(kill1, e0, imax, ic50, gamma),
    "E at 2-log" = imax_effect(kill2, e0, imax, ic50, gamma)
  )
fit_check |>
  select(drug, matrix, index, starts_with("E at")) |>
  rename(Drug = drug, Matrix = matrix, Index = index) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Equation 3 with the Tables S4-S6 parameters, evaluated at the Tables 2-4 targets (expected 0, -1, -2).")

consistent <- !(fits$drug == "LVFX" & fits$index == "Cmax/MIC") &
  !(fits$drug == "GRNX" & fits$index == "fCmax/MIC")
stopifnot(
  all(abs(fit_check$`E at stasis`[consistent]) < 0.06),
  all(abs(fit_check$`E at 1-log`[consistent] + 1) < 0.06),
  all(abs(fit_check$`E at 2-log`[consistent] + 2) < 0.06)
)
```

Sixteen of the eighteen fits reproduce their targets to within 0.05 log10
CFU/lung. The two that do not are discussed under Errata; neither is part of a
packaged model.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Mean of the per-dose fits.** The paper fitted each dose level separately
  and tabulates the three fits with their mean (Tables S1-S3). The packaged
  models use the mean, which is also the parameter set behind the paper's
  PK/PD indices: the lascufloxacin and garenoxacin ELF and plasma Imax fits
  differ only by an index scale factor that equals the mean-parameter AUC ratio
  (see "ELF penetration in the mouse"). The per-dose estimates are recorded on
  each `ini()` line. They vary more than two-fold for some parameters (for
  example levofloxacin plasma ka 7.10, 3.54 and 1.80 1/h), so the mean is a
  summary rather than a dose-independent fit.
- **Spread of the per-dose fits.** The 'SD' rows of Tables S1-S3 reproduce the
  population standard deviation of the three per-dose values for levofloxacin
  and lascufloxacin but not for garenoxacin (Table S2 prints 3.72 L/kg for
  plasma Vd, against 9.65 L/kg computed from 42.88, 19.48 and 28.34). The SD
  rows are not used by the models.
- **24 h index window.** The PK/PD indices are taken over the 24 h treatment
  window (doses from 2 to 26 h after infection, lungs harvested at 26 h), so
  the accumulators integrate from the first dose (t = 0) to t = 24 h and
  `dlog10cfu` is the paper's endpoint only when read at t = 24 h. Before that
  it reflects the exposure accumulated so far. The paper does not say whether
  the index of a late dose was AUC0-24 or AUC0-inf; for these short half-lives
  (0.8-3.7 h) the difference is small.
- **Free plasma, total ELF.** The plasma models predict total concentrations
  (`Cc`), and `Cu = fu * Cc` drives `fauc_0_24`, as the paper's index is
  fAUC/MIC. The ELF index is AUC/MIC of the urea-corrected ELF concentration
  with no unbound-fraction correction, as in the paper.
- **Separate plasma and ELF models.** The ELF data were fitted on their own
  ("PK analyses of the plasma and ELF concentrations were conducted
  separately"), so the ELF models have their own absorption rate constant
  draining the subcutaneous depot straight into `elf`, with no link to plasma.
  Simulate plasma and ELF with separate model instances.
- **Apparent volumes and clearances.** Subcutaneous bioavailability was not
  estimated, so every volume and clearance is apparent (V/F, CL/F).
- **Dose basis.** Garenoxacin was supplied as the mesilate hydrate and
  lascufloxacin as the hydrochloride; the paper does not say whether the mg/kg
  doses refer to the salt or the free base. The models take the dose as
  printed.
- **No variability.** The fits are naive-pooled least squares with no
  between-animal variability or residual error model reported, so the models
  carry no etas and a proportional residual SD held at zero. The Imax fits
  report only R^2, so `dlog10cfu` is a typical-value algebraic output with no
  residual error.
- **No baseline burden.** The paper reports only the change in lung burden,
  not the 2 h control count, so the models predict the change (`dlog10cfu`)
  rather than an absolute log10 CFU/lung.
- **Only the AUC/MIC fits are packaged.** fT>MIC and fCmax/MIC Imax fits were
  also reported (Tables S4-S6); AUC/MIC was the index most strongly correlated
  with the effect in both matrices, and the T>MIC and Cmax/MIC fits are
  reproduced in closed form above.

# Errata

- **Garenoxacin plasma fCmax/MIC, 2-log10 kill (Table 3).** The printed target
  is 28.9, but the Table S5 fit (Imax 4.07, IC50 2.37, E0 0.99, gamma 1.58)
  reaches -2 log10 CFU/lung at fCmax/MIC = 4.5 and gives -3.0 at 28.9. The
  stasis and 1-log10 targets of the same fit (1.2 and 2.3) reproduce. Figure 2C
  plots this curve flattening near -3 well before 15, consistent with a
  2-log10 target near 4.5; 28.9 appears to be a misprint.
- **Levofloxacin ELF Cmax/MIC IC50 (Table S4).** The printed IC50 is 55.71, but
  with it the curve stays at +0.40 log10 CFU/lung at every Table 2 target. An
  IC50 of 5.571 reproduces the Table 2 targets (3.4, 5.4 and 8.0) to within
  about 3%, and Figure 1F shows the curve reaching its plateau by a Cmax/MIC of
  about 10, so the decimal point appears to be misplaced.
- Neither discrepancy affects a packaged model. No correction notice for the
  paper was found in a EuropePMC search on 2026-11-16.
